edges.description: Strong constitutive FGFR3 signalling in growth-plate cartilage suppresses longitudinal endochondral bone growth. edges.description: Constitutive FGFR3 signalling in the developing telencephalon disturbs cortical neurogenesis and neuronal migration, most visibly in the temporal lobe. The direct genetic demonstration is in a mouse expressing the TD2 allele in cortical neurons; the human evidence is the constancy of the temporal-lobe malformation across both subtypes.

Acanthosis nigricans in TD survivors is attributed to FGFR3 activation in the skin, as in the other FGFR3 gain-of-function disorders that share it (SADDAN, Crouzon syndrome with acanthosis nigricans), and is not a consequence of insulin resistance. The epidermal intermediates are not curated here.
Short ribs and a small, bell-shaped thorax restrict the volume available for lung growth and for chest-wall excursion after birth.

Survivors have seizures, typically temporal-lobe epilepsy, attributed to the temporal-lobe malformation.

The cortical malformation is the main candidate substrate of the severe psychomotor delay of survivors, which persists despite respiratory support; hypoxic and craniocervical contributions are not excluded.

nodes.description: Because most affected infants die in the perinatal period from multisystem complications, management goals are set with the family and commonly focus on comfort care. Infants who are to be supported require long-term respiratory support, typically tracheostomy and ventilation. Anaesthetic guidelines for skeletal dysplasias apply. Other measures in long-term survivors include shunting for hydrocephalus, suboccipital decompression for craniocervical-junction constriction, anti-seizure medication and hearing aids.

nodes.description: A primary brain malformation, not a secondary effect of the skull. The temporal lobes show dysplasia with polymicrogyria, hippocampal abnormality and leptomeningeal glioneuronal heterotopia, with no detectable difference between TD1 and TD2, which is why it is curated at the root. Systematic autopsy series find it in every case once it is looked for, and it is the substrate of the temporal-lobe epilepsy and severe developmental delay of long-term survivors. Mouse work with the TD2 allele places FGFR3 activity directly in cortical neurogenesis and migration.

nodes.description: Every TD allele constitutively activates FGFR3 — ligand-independent receptor tyrosine phosphorylation and ligand-independent proliferative signalling — but the defining feature at the root level is that the TD alleles activate the receptor more strongly than the achondroplasia G380R allele does. This graded activation is the mechanistic basis of the FGFR3 severity gradient: hypochondroplasia (N540K), achondroplasia (G380R), SADDAN (K650M), thanatophoric dysplasia (R248C and related extracellular cysteine changes; K650E). Homozygous achondroplasia, which doubles the dose of a weaker allele, phenocopies TD — the dose-response corollary of the same claim. The receptor biology itself is held once in the `fgfr_gain_of_function_skeletal_dysplasia` module and is not re-derived here; see `Achondroplasia.yaml`, `Hypochondroplasia.yaml`, `SADDAN.yaml` and `Crouzon_Syndrome_with_Acanthosis_Nigricans.yaml` for the other points on the gradient.

nodes.description: Endochondral ossification fails throughout the appendicular and axial skeleton, producing extreme micromelia, platyspondyly and — critically — short ribs. Histologically the growth plate shows disordered ossification with chondrocyte hyperplasia and loss of the orderly proliferative columns. At the root level this node exists to carry the step from cartilage failure to the thoracic dimension; the zone-by-zone growth-plate detail belongs to the module and the subtype entries.

nodes.description: The step that makes thanatophoric dysplasia lethal, and the one part of the chain that is TD-specific rather than shared with the viable members of the FGFR3 allelic series. Severely shortened ribs and a narrow thorax restrict fetal lung growth and neonatal chest-wall excursion; respiratory insufficiency is the immediate cause of death in the great majority of affected infants. Survival beyond the perinatal period has been reported only with long-term tracheostomy and ventilation. This node is deliberately not anchored on the FGFR module: achondroplasia and hypochondroplasia share every upstream node and do not reach this one.
